Brave Bunnies is a Ukrainian children's animated television series for preschool children aged 2 to 5. Created by Olga Cherepanova, the series follows the adventures of two rabbit children, Bop and Boo, who show their courage and explore the world. The show is known for its themes of friendship and adventure, and has gained popularity worldwide.

The series was originally created by Ukrainian production Glowberry and premiered on major TV channels. It has since become one of the most popular children's television shows in dozens of countries. The show follows a family of bunnies, Bop and Boo, who go on a journey around the world to find new friends. At each stop, they discover different animals and create new games to help build new friendships.

The main characters of the series are Bop and Boo, two rabbit children who show their courage and explore the world. They are accompanied by their family and the Bunny Bus, which takes them on their adventures.

_**Brave Bunnies**_ ([Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_language "Ukrainian language"): Хоробрі зайці, [romanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Ukrainian "Romanization of Ukrainian"):_Khorobri zaitsi_) is a [Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_in_Ukraine "Television in Ukraine")[children's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children%27s_television_series "Children's television series")[animated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animated_series "Animated series") television series for [preschool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preschool "Preschool") children aged 2 to 5. In the series, two rabbit children show their courage when they meet and befriend other animals. Creator Olga Cherepanova sought to encourage respect for diversity and to promote healthy childhood development.

The series has been broadcast in more than 80 countries. The first season was produced by Glowberry and [Ánima Kitchent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81nima_(company) "Ánima (company)") in partnership with distributor [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations "Aardman Animations"), and premiered in December 2020. Production of the second season was interrupted by the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), and resumed in December 2022 after [WildBrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WildBrain "WildBrain") acquired a majority ownership of the property. A second season was distributed by WildBrain in 2023.

The 2D animated series follows the adventures of a family of rabbits:[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) Boo and Bop, Ma and Pa, and four Bunny Babies.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SartoBunnies-2) Every episode starts with a cheerful song as the family ride on their bunny bus, which stops at a new location. Brother Bop and sister Boo then explore and make friends with a different animal, creating a new game to play with them. The series attempts to show its preschool viewers the diversity of the world and to accept the differences of others.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) Starting in the second season, some episodes have the bunny family revisit friends at their homes, meeting their families and learning more about their different lifestyles.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)

The series introduces children to the concept of diversity and, through the example of the Brave Bunnies, shows how to accept and communicate with people possessing different appearances and behaviours.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguide-4)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) To promote healthy childhood development, characters Bop and Boo acknowledge the uniqueness of each new friend.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-WildbrainPrimary3-5)

The Ukrainian voice cast includes actress [Olena Kravets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olena_Kravets "Olena Kravets") and singer-songwriter [Potap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potap "Potap"), which [1+1 Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1%2B1_Media "1+1 Media") stated was the first time a Ukrainian children's animated series attracted such high-profile performers.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6)

*   Bop – Wilbur Conabeare (English dub)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Boo – Margot Powell (English dub)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bunny Ma – [Olena Kravets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olena_Kravets "Olena Kravets") (Ukrainian),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6) Harriet Kershaw (English dub)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bunny Pa – [Potap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potap "Potap") (Ukrainian),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6) Jensen Adeyanju (English dub)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)

Development and production
--------------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brave_Bunnies&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Development and production")]

Publishing house Glowberry was founded in 2009 and worked in children's literature and illustration,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-PrimaryGlowberry-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-FilmUA-9) seeking to create modern fairy tales. Their best-selling work was a picture book about a family of rabbits on a journey, meeting unusual animals as they travelled further from their home. Several years were spent developing this into a television series[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) for children aged 2 to 5.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3) Glowberry co-founder and series creator Olga Cherepanova[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) noted that while rabbits are often considered to be timid animals, their bravery in the series comes from discovering new challenges every day.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) She said that she created the series "to help children ... communicate with different friends without any fears or stereotypes, respecting the diversity of our world."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SartoBunnies-2)

Illustrator Anna Sarvira[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-13) developed the style for the series, serving as art director while Cherepanova was the creative producer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) Following this early creative work, the production became an international project to ensure funding, market access, and expertise. Over a hundred people in different countries were involved, coordinating together on the same schedule.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) This included British director Tim Fehrenbach and Canadian lead writer John Van Bruggen, both of whom had experience in children's animation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) Cherepanova was educated in psychology, and the writing team consulted with [child psychologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_psychology "Developmental psychology") throughout the process. They sought to maintain the interest of young children, present stories that would aid [early socialisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_socialization "Primary socialization"), and create characters representing the many different human [personality types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_type "Personality type").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) The music which celebrates the characters' achievements in each episode was composed in Ukraine.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)

In 2019, the series was in development with Glowberry and Ánima Kitchent (the Spanish subsidiary of Mexico-based animation studio [Ánima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81nima_(company) "Ánima (company)")).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-PulidoAnima-15) The production also received support from the [Ukrainian State Film Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_State_Film_Agency "Ukrainian State Film Agency") and the [Ministry of Youth and Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Youth_and_Sports_(Ukraine) "Ministry of Youth and Sports (Ukraine)").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-UkrinformItaly-16) Glowberry pitched the series to studios and distributors at [MIPCOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIPCOM "MIPCOM") in 2019. By early 2020, UK studio [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations "Aardman Animations") had partnered as the international distributor and secured additional international sales at the 2020 [Kidscreen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidscreen "Kidscreen") Summit in Miami.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) The first season consisted of 52 seven-minute episodes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1)

When the full-scale [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine") began in February 2022, the production of _Brave Bunnies_ in Kyiv was suspended.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YermakReporter-17) Many of the Glowberry team were forced to flee Kyiv,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) and production coordinator Natalia Yermak became a war correspondent for the _[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Times "New York Times")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YermakReporter-17) Production resumed in August[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) and by December 2022, Canadian children's entertainment company [WildBrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WildBrain "WildBrain") became a majority stakeholder in _Brave Bunnies_, to continue the reliable production and distribution of the series.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) WildBrain took over global distribution of the series, merchandising and licensing, and the company's Vancouver animation studio joined Glowberry and Ánima Kitchent[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-20) to produce the second season of 52 episodes.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TownsendWildbrain-21)

The series premiered on 5 December 2020 on [PLUSPLUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLUSPLUS "PLUSPLUS") in Ukraine, followed by [Nick Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Jr. "Nick Jr.") (UK), [Super RTL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_RTL "Super RTL") (Germany), [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_(Australian_TV_network) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)") (Australia), [Yle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yle "Yle") (Finland), and [HOP!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hop!_Channel "Hop! Channel") (Israel).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) The first season was distributed by Aardman Animations,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) and by 2022 had been broadcast in over 80 countries.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)

_Brave Bunnies_ streamed on the [Sunflower TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_TV "Sunflower TV") YouTube channel, which launched in July 2022 and allowed [Ukrainian refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_refugee_crisis "Ukrainian refugee crisis") across Europe and the UK to watch ad-free children's programming in the Ukrainian language.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MchughSunflower-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-EvansSunflower-23) Content was approved by a panel of media professionals, child psychologists and Ukrainian mothers. The creators of _Brave Bunnies_ along with partner companies waived their rights to enable the project.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MchughSunflower-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-EvansSunflower-23)

It is broadcast on WildBrain's [Family Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Jr. "Family Jr.") channel in Canada[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-BrzoznowskiWildbrain-24)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-BabieraWildbrain-25) and on the Comcast WildBrain+ [SVOD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_on_demand#Subscription_models "Video on demand") channel in the United States.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SenalWildbrain-18) The second season was released in Canada in June 2023[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TownsendWildbrain-21) followed by other territories later that year.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TodoWildbrain-26)

_Brave Bunnies_ was among the top-rated children's programs in Ukraine, the UK, Israel and Australia.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10)_[The New Voice of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Voice\_of\_Ukraine "The New Voice of Ukraine")_ applauded its message of diversity and acceptance.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14) A 2020 focus group by British research agency Childwise found that 79% of children aged 3 to 5 felt happier after watching the series, and 90% liked the characters.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)

Books and merchandising
-----------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brave_Bunnies&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Books and merchandising")]

Glowberry first distributed its books through the company's tablet app.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-FilmUA-9) Following the launch of the TV series, various publishers were licensed to print physical books for _Brave Bunnies_, beginning with Italian-language editions by [Planeta Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Agostini "De Agostini")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-UkrinformItaly-16)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-WildbrainPrimary3-5) in 2021.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14) English-language editions were published by [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House") imprint Ladybird Books. These children's books include picture books ([board books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_book "Board book")), [colouring books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloring_book "Coloring book"), [activity books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activity_book "Activity book"), and sticker books.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10)

Canadian multinational toy company [Spin Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_Master "Spin Master") created a line of toys for the franchise.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) The toy line includes figures, playsets, games, and plushies.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Toybook-27)
